newsitem.title: JAPAN: US port sanctions may not affect Japan car exports.
newsitem.headline: US port sanctions may not affect Japan car exports.

text.p: Japanese car exporters are unlikely to suffer any major damage from a U.S. decision to impose surcharges on Japanese shipping firms calling at U.S. ports, industry officials said on Thursday.

Spokesmen for Japanese auto companies said that the latest U.S. decision was unlikely to greatly affect their car exports, because the surcharge would be imposed only on container carriers and not on vessels transporting finished vehicles.

Although the surcharge will affect shipments of car parts to some degree, it will not hurt their overall businesses given the currently high local procurement rate at Japanese car makers' plants in the United States.
Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mitsubishi, Mazda, Isuzu and Fuji Heavy have U.S. units that produce autos with local content rates ranging from 65 percent to 91 percent.

On Wednesday, the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission said it would impose $100,000 port surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports in response to what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices" at Japanese ports. The surcharge will take effect on April 14.

The surcharge will be imposed each time a vessel owned or operated by Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK enters a U.S. port from abroad, but not from another U.S. port, it said.

In January, Japanese car exports to the United States rose a steep 75 percent from a year earlier to 124,834 units. It was the fifth straight month of year-on-year gains caused by a weaker yen, industry data showed.
